hypothesis: The selected two-feature pairwise reranker over the strongest validated dialogue and retrieval stack is the best recoverable control.
mechanism: Compile the research policy and its fold-safe learned ranking parameters into the official adapter.
diagnosis: This is the current control, not a claim of global optimality. Research-versus-compiled parity and runtime checks passed; the protected holdout remains sealed.

hypothesis: A short, deterministic sequence of high-yield clarification questions improves retrieval while limiting time-to-correct.
mechanism: Ask the validated raw-history question sequence and stop once the policy has enough evidence.
diagnosis: The raw sequence remained the strongest tested dialogue controller after retrieval and ranking changed. It is a strong static control, not an adaptive learned policy.

hypothesis: Observable uncertainty rules can choose a better next question than a fixed order.
mechanism: Select the next missing field using hand-authored ambiguity and candidate-coverage signals.
diagnosis: Hand-authored adaptivity did not beat the tuned raw static sequence. Retest only after stronger state parsing or learned counterfactual values can supply a materially different signal.
retest_conditions: A fold-safe learned action-value model exists.
Structured state extraction improves independently without leaking target labels.

hypothesis: A fold-safe action-value model can learn which legal question or stop action maximizes final technical reward for each state.
mechanism: Generate counterfactual legal actions in the simulator, learn Q(state, action) only from training folds, and choose the best legal action at inference.
diagnosis: Planned advanced challenger. It must be compared with the static champion and a heuristic adaptive control; simulator shortcuts and fold leakage are the primary risks.

hypothesis: Keeping the user's raw answers preserves useful lexical evidence with minimal parsing error.
mechanism: Accumulate normalized raw conversation history and append it to the retrieval query.
diagnosis: Raw history was more robust than the tested structured summaries and became the dialogue-state control. It can coexist with a future structured channel rather than being replaced.

hypothesis: Explicit preferences, constraints, overrides, and negative evidence enable safer adaptive decisions than raw text alone.
mechanism: Parse turns into typed multi-valued fields while retaining provenance and the raw-history channel.
diagnosis: Structured multi-value state helped the early fixed baseline but later lost to raw history end to end. Preserve it for interactions with learned questioning, query construction, and negative-evidence handling; do not replace raw history by default.
retest_conditions: Evaluate as a parallel feature channel, not as a destructive summary of raw history.

hypothesis: Separate raw, positive-constraint, and negative-constraint query channels can preserve recall while giving the ranker cleaner semantics.
mechanism: Build non-destructive lexical and semantic subqueries from raw history plus typed state, then expose their scores and conflicts as features.
diagnosis: Planned challenger. It must preserve the raw channel because replacing it with summaries previously reduced score.

hypothesis: Field-aware lexical retrieval is a strong low-latency candidate generator for catalog search.
mechanism: Weight indexed title, feature, category, and related catalog fields with BM25-style lexical evidence.
diagnosis: Feature-field weighting produced a clear gain, and selected field interactions improved it further. This remains the retrieval control for semantic challengers.

hypothesis: Generic dense embeddings rescue semantically relevant products missed by sparse retrieval.
mechanism: Embed queries and catalog text with MiniLM and retrieve by vector similarity.
diagnosis: Generic dense retrieval was weaker alone and its tested fusions reduced end-to-end score, but it supplied 17 dense-only hits and raised union Recall@200 to 0.846667. This is evidence of complementarity, not evidence to ship MiniLM unchanged.
retest_conditions: Use a stronger retrieval-specific model or domain-adapted representation.
Evaluate candidate recall and full-policy reward separately.

hypothesis: A retrieval-trained embedding model with field-aware document text can turn observed dense-only recall into useful ranked candidates.
mechanism: Index normalized catalog documents with a retrieval-specific encoder, validate model assets offline, and expose dense scores to fusion and reranking.
diagnosis: Planned semantic challenger. Its value must be established first at candidate recall, then end to end under runtime and memory constraints.

hypothesis: Combining sparse and dense ranks recovers complementary candidates while retaining strong lexical results.
mechanism: Fuse sparse and dense candidate lists with reciprocal-rank or calibrated weighted-score fusion.
diagnosis: Both tested RRF and weighted fusion lost to keyword retrieval end to end. Retest only after the dense model improves; fusion cannot repair a weak component through weight search alone.
retest_conditions: Dense candidate recall or ranking quality improves materially over MiniLM.
Fusion weights are selected inside training folds.

hypothesis: Observable query features can route each session to the retrieval method most likely to help.
mechanism: Fit a fold-safe shallow route policy from query and state features, never oracle target information.
diagnosis: The observable stump selected keyword for every session; richer simple features were worse. The oracle gap shows opportunity, but no tested observable router captured it.
retest_conditions: Retrieval components are both competitive enough to create learnable routing labels.
Use grouped out-of-fold route labels and compare with always-sparse.

hypothesis: Hard filtering explicit constraints improves precision when state extraction is reliable.
mechanism: Apply only high-confidence constraints whose catalog coverage is sufficient; otherwise retain candidates and use soft ranking features.
diagnosis: The tested filter slightly hurt the strongest raw-history policy, consistent with false exclusions. Retest only with provenance, confidence, and coverage guards.
retest_conditions: Parser precision and catalog coverage guards are measured out of fold.
A no-hard-filter fallback is always available.

hypothesis: Profile preferences can break ties among otherwise relevant candidates.
mechanism: Add a fixed profile-similarity prior to retrieval scores.
diagnosis: Even the smallest tested fixed prior reduced score, with larger weights degrading monotonically. Retest profile evidence only as a learned, gated feature that yields to explicit session intent.
retest_conditions: The ranker can gate profile evidence by explicit current-session constraints.
All profile weights are learned inside folds.

hypothesis: A small catalog-quality prior improves ordering among products with similar relevance evidence.
mechanism: Add the selected low-weight quality score after field-aware lexical scoring.
diagnosis: Quality weight 0.2 improved the validated triple-field scorer and remained useful in later rechecks. It is a bounded tie-breaking signal, not a substitute for relevance.

hypothesis: A manually weighted lexical reranker improves product order beyond retrieval scores.
mechanism: Apply a fixed linear combination of lexical and state-match features.
diagnosis: The tested fixed linear reranker did not improve the strongest raw-history control. Keep the feature ideas, but do not ship this hand-weighted variant.
retest_conditions: Only retest through fold-safe learned weights or materially different features.

hypothesis: A compact pairwise learner can improve item ordering and time-to-correct without an unnecessarily broad feature set.
mechanism: Fit fold-safe pairwise logistic weights over the selected feature and quality signals, then refit on all development sessions for compilation.
diagnosis: The two-feature model was selected because it stayed within 0.01 of the best OOF score, retained higher Hit@10, and used fewer features than the full model. This favors robustness over the largest decimal.

hypothesis: A constrained gradient-boosted ranker can capture nonlinear interactions among lexical, semantic, state, quality, and profile features.
mechanism: Train a grouped pairwise ranking objective inside each fold with depth, leaf, and early-stopping limits; compare against the linear champion.
diagnosis: Planned advanced challenger. The small development set makes shallow capacity controls, grouped folds, and honest nested selection mandatory.

hypothesis: A compact cross-encoder can resolve semantic relevance among a small top-candidate set better than independent query and document embeddings.
mechanism: Rerank only the top K candidates using joint query-product text, with offline assets, bounded latency, and fold-safe calibration or tuning.
diagnosis: Planned advanced challenger. It is an expensive reranker, not a full-catalog retriever; latency, memory, and model licensing are gating criteria.

hypothesis: An adaptive family allocator spends more trials on promising mutation families than a fixed search schedule.
mechanism: Allocate trial probability from observed family gains plus an exploration bonus.
diagnosis: At the tested equal budget, grid search found the better candidate. Keep evidence-weighted allocation as research infrastructure, but do not assume it produces a better policy without another controlled comparison.
retest_conditions: The search space contains enough heterogeneous families for adaptive allocation to matter.
Compare under identical candidate and wall-clock budgets.

hypothesis: Deterministic bounded enumeration is the most auditable discovery control for the current small search space.
mechanism: Use staged grid or beam search with predeclared budgets, cached replay, and fold-aware validation.
diagnosis: Grid search was strongest at the compared budgets and is easier to reproduce. It does not prove exhaustive global optimality; interactions still require a bounded compatibility matrix.

hypothesis: Explicit dislikes and rejected constraints prevent the policy from repeatedly retrieving incompatible products.
mechanism: Store typed negative constraints separately from positive intent, with turn provenance, confidence, and override semantics.
diagnosis: Removing negative evidence hurt the tested structured policy, so the signal matters inside that representation. Its contribution has not yet been isolated on the final raw-history champion.
retest_conditions: Retain raw history and evaluate typed negatives as an additional channel.
Test override and contradiction behavior explicitly.

hypothesis: Avoiding clarification minimizes conversational cost enough to compensate for weaker intent evidence.
mechanism: Return retrieval results without asking a clarification question.
diagnosis: No-question policies lose too much relevance under this evaluator. The valid optimization target is when to stop asking, not whether clarification can be removed entirely.
retest_conditions: Use only as the stop-action control inside a learned policy.

hypothesis: Learned sparse semantic expansion can add synonym recall while preserving lexical exact-match behavior and inspectability.
mechanism: Generate sparse expansion weights with an offline model, then merge the resulting terms or scores with field-aware BM25.
diagnosis: A meaningful semantic alternative to dense retrieval that is not yet implemented. It should be tested only if its model asset and runtime fit the competition environment.

hypothesis: A minimal learned ranker using only the quality feature generalizes better than a broader feature set.
mechanism: Fit the pairwise learner with only catalog quality enabled.
diagnosis: It had the largest scalar OOF score in the feature ablation but lower Hit@10 and worse MTTC than the selected two-feature model. It remains a documented near-champion, not the control, because the predeclared robustness rule preferred Hit@10 and feature stability within the 0.01 score band.
retest_conditions: Re-evaluate across repeated grouped splits before reconsidering promotion.

hypothesis: A shallow grouped LambdaMART reranker can learn stable interactions among rank, lexical coverage, quality, and explicit metadata missingness beyond the two-feature linear champion.
mechanism: Fit deterministic depth-capped boosted regression trees from grouped LambdaRank derivatives; keep complete sessions and all their turns together, select stopping rounds only inside each outer-training side, and serialize a NumPy-only runtime model.
diagnosis: The candidate improved all five outer folds and produced a +0.043767 paired session-reward delta with bootstrap interval [0.016708, 0.073183]. Rank-only reproduced the fixed field+quality control, while lexical and metadata variants isolated the nonlinear gain. Runtime and packaging passed. Promote to integration without modifying the compiled champion; confirm the variable fold-local stopping rounds and the smaller all-development refit gain during integration.

hypothesis: The precommitted median of the five fold-local stopping rounds yields a deterministic and packageable all-development refit without outcome-driven round aggregation.
mechanism: Freeze 56 rounds before amended evaluation, refit the selected metadata model twice on all 150 adaptive sessions, compare serialized bytes and session outcomes, and run executable scenario, fold, parity, failure, and packaging gates.
diagnosis: This is deployment-fit verification, not independent generalization evidence. The nested OOF family score remains 0.861417. Two independent 56-round refits were byte-identical, per-session outcomes matched, isolated runtime parity passed, and 353 instrumented responses produced zero failures. This version supersedes the initial four-round deployment artifact without changing the compiled champion.

hypothesis: Deterministic runtime-observable structured state can improve the audited metadata GBDT by separating active constraint coverage from negative, neutral, provenance, invalidation, turn, and retrieval-confidence context.
mechanism: Augment the frozen depth-3 metadata LambdaMART with active positive coverage count/ratio, explicit-negative contradiction, neutral no-preference, explicit/simulator provenance coverage, invalidation-only context, turn, sparse margin, and sparse entropy features. Keep the Top-50 head, folds, fixed question flow, tree capacity, and audited fold round counts unchanged.
diagnosis: The precommitted single candidate improved four of five folds and every aggregate scenario. Paired bootstrap 95% interval [0.006970, 0.041826], randomization p=0.006599, and 42/87/21 wins/ties/losses support a real interaction rather than a scalar search accident. Active constraint coverage ratio dominated the added split usage; invalidation context and retrieval confidence also appeared, while negative/no-preference fields were available but not selected. This is grouped OOF evidence, not proof for the private set; the one negative fold and small Boundary slice remain explicit risks.
retest_conditions: Recheck paired and backward-ablation behavior after any question-policy or retrieval-head change.
Run isolated latency after concurrent experiments finish before integration runtime sign-off.

hypothesis: The original v1 constraint interaction used correct observable state and runtime semantics.
mechanism: Independent semantic, training/runtime parity, and concurrent-context audit of the v1 implementation and report.
diagnosis: Reject D028 as promotion evidence. Intent-override messages left stale non-category preferences active when replacement attributes differed; training duplicated consecutive other questions while runtime deduplicated them; and mutable bound runtime context was unsafe across concurrent sessions. The numeric result is preserved only for provenance and must not be used for selection.
retest_conditions: Use only the precommitted scoped-correction v2 retest.

hypothesis: Corrected scoped runtime state retains a stable constraint-aware GBDT gain without Hit or scenario regressions.
mechanism: Rerun the unchanged constraint feature block and frozen depth-3 GBDT protocol after scoped override invalidation, exact question-bookkeeping parity, and invocation-scoped concurrent runtime context repairs.
diagnosis: The corrected candidate improved four of five folds, but its paired interval [-0.007212, 0.035689] crossed zero (p=0.182982). It failed frozen robustness gates: overall Hit@10 delta was -0.006666 and intent-override scenario reward delta was -0.018279. Preserve the real MRR gain, but do not promote this unguarded interaction. The all-development score is deployment-fit only.
retest_conditions: Retest only after a precommitted observable override guard or a materially changed question/retrieval dependency.
